### Caesarstone Reports Third Quarter 2026 Financial Results


November 11, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s23.q4cdn.com/225400014/files/doc_news/Caesarstone-Reports-Third-Quarter-2026-Financial-Results-2026.pdf)


**- Revenue of $96.3 Million and Gross Margin of 25.4% -**


**- Net loss of $56.1 million reflecting $46.8 Million Related to California Jury Verdict -**


**- Adjusted Net loss of $1.6 million and Delivers Near Breakeven Adjusted EBITDA -**


MP MENASHE, Israel--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


Caesarstone Ltd. (NASDAQ: CSTE), a leading developer and manufacturer of high-quality engineered surfaces, today reported financial results for its third quarter ended September 30, 2026.


Yos Shiran, Caesarstone’s Chief Executive Officer commented, “Our underlying business performed well as we continued to execute our strategic plan. Gross margin improved year-over-year for the third consecutive quarter, reaching 25.4%. We also delivered near breakeven Adjusted EBITDA reflecting the benefits of our optimized production network and the cost savings from our restructuring plan. While the U.S. market remains soft, we saw stabilization in Canada and continued growth in Australia as we rebuild our position in that important market. Separately, we strongly disagree with the recent jury verdict in California and will consider our available post-trial remedies as we evaluate its impact on our business.”


**Third Quarter 2026 Results**


**Revenue** in the third quarter of 2026 was $96.3 million compared to $102.1 million in the prior year quarter. On a constant currency basis, third quarter revenue was lower by approximately 7.2% year-over-year, reflecting continued softness in global demand and competitive pressures, particularly in the U.S., partially offset by strength in Australia.


**Gross margin** in the third quarter of 2026 was 25.4% compared to 17.3% in the prior year quarter. Adjusted gross margin in the third quarter was 26.9%, compared to 17.3% in the prior year quarter. The improvement in gross margin mainly reflects the realization of cost savings associated with the Company’s transition to its global network of production partners following the closure of its Bar-Lev facility. The third quarter also benefited from a refund received on account of previously paid U.S. IEEPA tariffs.


**Operating expenses** in the third quarter of 2026 were $81.4 million, or 84.6% of revenue, compared to $33.7 million, or 33.0% of revenue in the prior year quarter. The year-over-year difference primarily reflects higher legal settlements and loss contingencies which includes the impact of the recent California jury verdict. Excluding legal settlements and loss contingencies and impairment and restructuring expenses, operating expenses were 28.8% of revenue compared to 29.1% in the prior year quarter.


**Operating loss** in the third quarter of 2026 was $56.9 million compared to an operating loss of $16.0 million in the prior year quarter. The decline was primarily driven by higher operating expenses primarily related to legal settlements and loss contingencies.


**Adjusted EBITDA** in the third quarter of 2026, which excludes expenses for non-cash share-based compensation, legal settlements and loss contingencies, impairment and restructuring charges and other non-recurring items, was a loss of $0.1 million compared to a loss of $7.9 million in the prior year quarter. The improvement primarily reflects higher gross margin and the benefits of the Company’s cost savings initiatives.


**Finance income** in the third quarter of 2026 was $1.2 million compared to finance expenses of $1.8 million in the prior year quarter. The difference primarily reflects foreign currency exchange rate fluctuations.


**Net loss attributable to controlling interest** for the third quarter of 2026 was $56.1 million, compared to $18.1 million in the prior year quarter. Net loss per share for the third quarter of 2026 was $1.62 compared to a net loss per share of $0.52 in the prior year quarter. Adjusted diluted net loss per share for the third quarter was $0.05 on 35.0 million shares, compared to an Adjusted diluted net loss per share of $0.40 in the prior year quarter on 34.6 million shares.


**Balance Sheet & Liquidity**


As of September 30, 2026, the Company’s balance sheet included cash, cash equivalents and short-term bank deposits of $50.7 million and no debt to financial institutions compared to a net cash position of $51.8 million as of June 30, 2026.


**U.S. Tariffs Update**


The Company continues to monitor the impact of existing and proposed U.S. tariffs affecting various countries and product categories, that are currently in a wide range on the majority of products imported into the U.S. Approximately 40% of the Company’s revenues during the three months ended September 30, 2026 were generated in the U.S. market, served by the Company’s global production network.


In addition to other tariffs, on July 31, 2026, the U.S. Administration issued its final determination imposing a four-year tariff-rate quota on imports of quartz surface products, effective August 15, 2026. During the first year, the industry’s covered imports within an annual quota of approximately 13.0 million square meters, assessed quarterly, will be subject to an additional 25% tariff, while imports exceeding the quota will be subject to an additional 50% tariff. During the subsequent three years, the tariff rates will gradually decline, while the annual quota will gradually increase.


The Company estimates the annualized impact of the additional tariffs under the tariff-rate quota, which apply on top of existing tariffs, to be in the range of $10.0 million to $15.0 million. The Company implemented pricing actions in the U.S. in September 2026 and is evaluating further supply-chain and sourcing actions to mitigate the impact of these tariffs.


**Legal Proceedings Update**


Caesarstone Ltd. (the “Company”) and its subsidiaries, including Caesarstone USA, Inc., are defendants in approximately 870 individual suits alleging injuries related to exposure to silica particles while fabricating the Company’s products, including approximately 670 claims in the U.S. The Company is unable to estimate the potential exposure related to the majority of such claims in the U.S. since they are either at an early stage or considered only reasonably possible losses, and therefore no provision has been recorded in connection therewith.


On October 26, 2026, the jury rendered a verdict in one such case brought in the Superior Court of California, *Dennys Rene Rivas-Williams v. A&A Granite Marble, et al.* The jury found the Company liable and awarded the plaintiff approximately $67.3 million in damages. The Company was apportioned 69.1% of the fault, or approximately $46.8 million, if assessed without modification.


The Company strongly disagrees with the jury’s verdict. It believes the verdict is not supported by the facts of the case or the applicable law, including the fault attributable to the plaintiff’s employer, and that the trial included significant legal errors and will consider its available post-trial remedies.


The jury verdict has created significant uncertainty regarding the Company’s financial condition and prospects and raises substantial doubt about its ability to continue as a going concern in the ordinary course. The Company is evaluating the impact of the verdict on its business, results of operations, liquidity and financial condition and is considering its alternatives.


During October, the Company resolved additional claims in California. Prior verdicts remain under appeal.


In addition, the Company and certain of its insurers in the U.S. are in litigation to determine coverage, and therefore there is no assurance as to the availability of coverage under the Company’s insurance policies. The Company intends to continue to vigorously defend these claims and to continue to seek its rights to coverage.


As of September 30, 2026, the Company recorded a provision of $105.5 million, representing its best estimate of probable and reasonably estimable losses associated with legal proceedings. As of September 30, 2026 the Company recorded $13.6 million of insurance receivables related to claims in Israel and Australia.


Additional information related to legal proceedings can be found in the Company's Annual Report on Form 20-F for the year ended December 31, 2025.

**About Caesarstone**


Caesarstone is a global leader of premium surfaces, specializing in countertops that create dynamic spaces of inspiration in the heart of the home. Established in 1987, its multi-material portfolio of over 100 colors combines the company’s innovative technology with its powerful design passion. Spearheading high-quality, sustainable surfaces, Caesarstone delivers functional resilience with timeless beauty, for a vast range of applications, including kitchen countertops, bathroom vanities, and more, for indoor and outdoor spaces.


Since it pioneered quartz countertops over thirty years ago, the brand has expanded into porcelain and natural stone and is on the ground in more than 50 countries worldwide while enhancing customer experience through the expansion of groundbreaking digital platforms & services. More information on Caesarstone:[caesarstoneus.com,](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fcaesarstoneus.com%2F&esheet=54638898&newsitemid=20261111609249&lan=en-US&anchor=caesarstoneus.com%2C&index=2&md5=ce3cc6433494da60989fe19d5064e542)[Facebook](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.facebook.com%2FCaesarstoneUS%2F&esheet=54638898&newsitemid=20261111609249&lan=en-US&anchor=Facebook&index=3&md5=0fddcd324cdd7d8576979d1edb06cb09) ,[LinkedIn](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.linkedin.com%2Fcompany%2Fcaesarstoneus%2F&esheet=54638898&newsitemid=20261111609249&lan=en-US&anchor=LinkedIn&index=4&md5=45d1f9157ff96805b45c69dbff26ab9d) and[Instagram](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.instagram.com%2Fcaesarstoneus&esheet=54638898&newsitemid=20261111609249&lan=en-US&anchor=Instagram&index=5&md5=47e2a484670b36f10be20e01066afe6e)

**Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


The non-GAAP measures presented by the Company should be considered in addition to, and not as a substitute for, comparable GAAP measures. Reconciliations of GAAP gross profit to Adjusted gross profit, GAAP net income (loss) to Adjusted net income (loss) and net income (loss) to Adjusted EBITDA are provided in the schedules to this release. To calculate revenues growth rates that exclude the impact of changes in foreign currency exchange rates, the Company converts actual reported results from local currency to U.S. dollars using constant foreign currency exchange rates in the current and comparable period. The Company provides these non-GAAP financial measures because it believes that they present a better measure of the Company's core business and management uses the non-GAAP measures internally to evaluate the Company's ongoing performance. Accordingly, the Company believes that they are useful to investors in enhancing an understanding of the Company's operating performance.

Such forward-looking statements include statements regarding the Company’s goals and plans, intentions, expectations, assumptions, goals and beliefs regarding the Company’s business. Actual results may differ materially from those projections and estimates due to various risks and uncertainties, both known or unknown. These factors include, but are not limited to: the effects of the global and regional economy and geo-politics on the Company’s business and operations including the length, duration and impact of the war in Israel, the Houthi’s disruption to the movement of goods in the Red Sea and trade disruptions such as Turkey’s decision not to trade with Israel; the outcome of silicosis and other bodily injury claims, including appeals and post-trial remedies, and the availability of relevant insurance; regulatory changes and requirements relating to the manufacturing and fabrication of our products; the outcome of our restructuring efforts, of the closure of the Sdot Yam and Richmond Hill Facilities, the estimated closure costs and the estimated potential savings relating to said closures, the ability to sell or sublease all or part of these facilities; our ability to effectively collaborate with production business partners; our R&D and product introduction efforts, managing constraints in the global supply chain and effectively procuring raw materials and goods as well as fluctuations in their price; our ability to mitigate the recently imposed U.S. customs tariffs; our ability to protect our brand, technology and intellectual property, as well as our freedom to operate; competitive pressures; disruptions to our information technology systems, fluctuations in currency exchange rates against the U.S. dollar;
